chunks: The Sheikh (may God support him) informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS), who said:

The Messenger of God (SAWW) was the most scrupulous of all people in guarding against urine. When he wished to urinate, he would head toward an elevated area of ground, or toward a place among places where there was abundant soil, out of aversion to urine being splashed back onto him.
Then he said: And he [the Prophet] would not face the wind with his urine, for it [the wind] would reverse it and send it back onto his body and his clothes.

key_terms.اَلْبَوْلِ: urine; a primary source of najasah (ritual impurity) in Islamic law
key_terms.تَوَقِّياً: scrupulous avoidance, vigilant guarding against (najasah contamination)
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةَ: out of aversion to; causal adverbial indicating deliberate avoidance
key_terms.يُنْضَحَ: to be splashed back, to be sprinkled upon (passive form)

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet Muhammad's practice for protecting himself from urine splashback according to Imam al-Sadiq in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, this hadith describes the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) as the most scrupulous of all people in guarding against urine contamination (najasah). He would seek elevated ground or soil-rich terrain to prevent splashback, and would not urinate facing the wind, as it would return the urine to his body and garments. The hadith reflects the Prophetic sunnah of meticulous taharah that underpins the Shia fiqh rulings collected in this chapter of Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
